description: Find the JSON defects that corrupt data silently: integers beyond 2^53-1 that a double-based reader cannot represent, numbers with more significant digits than a double round-trips, keys repeated inside one object (reported with that object's path), non-standard NaN and Infinity literals, and content after the document ends. Choose this when a JSON document crosses a language boundary and a large integer, an imprecise float or a repeated key could be changed silently with no parser error. Do not choose this when the document should be validated against a schema (use json-schema-validation) or its key naming audited (use json-key-audit). Example requests: Is this JSON safe to parse in JavaScript without losing precision? | Does this JSON have duplicate keys? | Why does my 64-bit id lose precision when my app reads this API response?
